note: SCOPE_1.7.3 §2(a), §0 contracts 3-4, and §8. A cloud ride is a parent document plus N ordered chunk documents; the parent carries chunkCount and is written last. Chunk ids are zero-padded so lexical order is chronological order. §8 names this as the contract worth pinning: a client that formats `1` where the other formats `001` uploads rides the other platform silently reassembles in the wrong order, or cannot find at all. Invisible until someone switches phone.
rules: The parent is the commit marker AND the tombstone: written last on upload, deleted last on removal.
Children are written before the parent and deleted before the parent — strict reverse order.
Readers take exactly chunkCount chunks and ignore anything beyond, so a stale orphan from a re-upload is inert before it is cleaned up.
Reassembly order is built from chunkCount, not from a sorted query. Padding keeps every other view of the data (console, orderBy(documentId()), export tooling) honest.
A ride whose parent carries chunkCount but whose chunks are incomplete must be REJECTED, not partially imported. Half a ride that looks plausible is worse than no ride.

chunkIds.note: Past 999 the id grows a fourth digit and lexical order no longer matches chronological order. Reassembly is unaffected because it is built from chunkCount, never sorted. 999 chunks is 999,000 points — about eleven days of continuous 1 Hz recording. Both clients must agree on this behaviour rather than one of them clamping.

chunkCounts.note: no points is no chunks, not one empty chunk — an empty chunk document is a read that always returns nothing
